referenceLabel: modern US pennies
singularLabel: a modern US penny
assumption: One copper-plated zinc US penny has a nominal mass of 2.50 g (0.0025 kg); this does not describe older copper pennies.
sourceNote: US Mint's 2025 penny specifications list 2.50 g. Use the zinc circulating coin, not the gold commemorative.

referenceLabel: unweighted Logitech G502 HERO mice
singularLabel: an unweighted Logitech G502 HERO mouse
assumption: One Logitech G502 HERO mouse has a baseline chassis mass of 121 g (0.121 kg), without its optional tuning weights.
sourceNote: Manufacturer comparison explicitly gives a baseline of 121 g, rising to 139 g with added weights. This is chassis mass, not a packaged product.

referenceLabel: original-model Nintendo Switch 2 consoles with controllers
singularLabel: an original-model Nintendo Switch 2 with both controllers attached
assumption: The Nintendo Switch 2 version without a user-replaceable battery weighs approximately 534 g (0.534 kg) with both Joy-Con 2 controllers attached.
sourceNote: Nintendo's specifications distinguish 534 g with controllers for the non-user-replaceable-battery model from 548 g for the user-replaceable-battery model. This reference selects the former.

referenceLabel: 16-pound bowling balls
singularLabel: a 16-pound bowling ball
assumption: The reference is explicitly a 16 lb bowling ball: 16 x 0.45359237 kg = 7.25747792 kg. It is not an average ball.
sourceNote: PBA rules set 16.00 lb as the maximum ball weight. We define a ball at that weight; the pound-to-kilogram conversion is exact.

referenceLabel: roughly 40-kilogram Parmesan wheels
singularLabel: a roughly 40-kilogram wheel of Parmesan
assumption: One Parmigiano Reggiano wheel is approximated as 40 kg, the average cited in the consortium's glossary; individual wheels vary.
sourceNote: The official consortium glossary's Wheel entry gives average mass as 40 kg. This rounded estimate must not be presented as an exact specification for every wheel.

referenceLabel: Cat 797F mining trucks at rated gross weight
singularLabel: a Cat 797F mining truck at rated gross weight
assumption: One Cat 797F at its rated gross machine weight is approximately 623,690 kg, including its load. This is not the empty truck mass.
sourceNote: Caterpillar's Weights - Approximate table lists rated gross machine weight 623690 kg, separately from chassis weight and payload.

referenceLabel: the rated power of a Breville Smart Kettle Clear
singularLabel: a Breville Smart Kettle Clear at its rated power
assumption: One Australian Breville Smart Kettle Clear BKE840 is rated at 2,400 W. Energy scenes assume it draws that power throughout; this does not specify water heated or boil time.
sourceNote: Breville's current page returned HTTP 200. Its Product JSON-LD explicitly lists Power as 2400 Watts for the Australian BKE840.

referenceLabel: the rated power of a Dyson Supersonic hair dryer
singularLabel: a Dyson Supersonic hair dryer at its rated power
assumption: One US-market Dyson Supersonic hair dryer is rated at 1,600 W. Energy scenes assume constant rated input; actual draw varies with its settings.
sourceNote: Dyson's specifications list 120 V and 1,600 W. The rating is not a measurement of useful heat reaching hair.

referenceLabel: the rated power of an Adventure two-slice toaster
singularLabel: a Russell Hobbs Adventure two-slice toaster at its rated power
assumption: One Russell Hobbs Adventure two-slice toaster, model 24080-56, is rated at 850 W. Energy scenes assume constant rated input and do not imply a number of cooked slices.
sourceNote: Manufacturer product page specifies 850 Watt; model and rating also appear in its SS22 catalogue.

referenceLabel: the maximum power of an RTC Vectron MS locomotive
singularLabel: an RTC Vectron MS locomotive at maximum power
assumption: The Vectron MS locomotives ordered by RTC have a stated maximum power of 6.4 MW (6,400,000 W). This is a maximum locomotive rating, not measured electrical consumption.
sourceNote: Siemens' 3 June 2025 release states maximum power 6.4 megawatts. Do not treat this as an electrical-input or electricity-generation primitive.

referenceLabel: the measured average power of docked Mario Kart World
singularLabel: a docked Nintendo Switch 2 playing Mario Kart World
assumption: Nintendo reports about 19 W average power during active Mario Kart World gaming in TV mode, averaged over Full HD and 4K. A duration calculation assumes that constant average; it excludes the TV.
sourceNote: Nintendo specifies TV-mode active gaming 19 W, measured with Mario Kart World, averaged over Full HD and 4K; values are rounded and vary with usage conditions.

referenceLabel: Dippy dinosaur replicas laid head to tail
singularLabel: a Dippy dinosaur replica from head to tail
assumption: The Natural History Museum's Dippy Diplodocus replica measures 26 m from head to tail; this is the exhibit, not an average living dinosaur.
sourceNote: The museum article returned HTTP 200 on direct retrieval and states that Dippy measures 26 metres from head to tail and is a cast of Diplodocus fossil bones.

referenceLabel: short-wheelbase Enviro400 double-decker buses
singularLabel: a 10.5-metre Enviro400 double-decker bus
assumption: The shortest Enviro400 version in Alexander Dennis' July 2023 specification is 10.5 m long; other offered versions are longer.
sourceNote: Manufacturer datasheet page 2 offers lengths 10.5, 10.9 and 11.5 m. This reference selects the 10.5 m model explicitly.

referenceLabel: Eiffel Tower heights including the antenna
singularLabel: the Eiffel Tower's full height including its antenna
assumption: The Eiffel Tower's stated current overall height is 330 m, including its antenna; the public upper floor is lower.
sourceNote: Official operator's key figures list current height 330 metres and third floor 276 metres separately. No claim that a visitor can stand at 330 m.

referenceLabel: 330-millilitre cans of Coca-Cola
singularLabel: a 330-millilitre can of Coca-Cola
assumption: One explicitly 330 mL can contains 0.00033 cubic metres of drink. This is liquid content, not the can's exterior volume.
sourceNote: Coca-Cola's own FAQ identifies a 330 ml can. Millilitres-to-cubic-metres conversion is exact; no claim that every market uses this size.

referenceLabel: 50-litre beer keg fills
singularLabel: a 50-litre beer keg fill
assumption: A 50 L SCHAEFER PLUS KEG has a nominal liquid capacity of 0.05 cubic metres. This counts contents, not the exterior vessel volume.
sourceNote: SCHAEFER explicitly offers a 50 litre PLUS KEG. This reference selects that nominal size from several available sizes.

referenceLabel: 60-inch Sterling Spectacle bathtub capacities
singularLabel: a 60-inch Sterling Spectacle bathtub at its stated water capacity
assumption: The 60-by-32-inch Sterling Spectacle bathtub has a stated water capacity of 65 US gallons, about 0.246052 cubic metres. This is its capacity, not an average person's bathwater use.
sourceNote: Sterling's US product announcement returned HTTP 200 and specifies 65 gallons for the 60-by-32-inch model, separately from 79 gallons for the larger model. Exact US-gallon conversion: 65 x 0.003785411784 m^3.

referenceLabel: 2023 US Flag postage-stamp footprints
singularLabel: a 2023 US Flag postage-stamp footprint
assumption: The 2023 US Flag stamp is 0.87 by 0.98 inches; its rectangular footprint is 0.000550063416 square metres. This excludes gaps between stamps.
sourceNote: USPS Stamp Announcement 23-16 gives stamp size 22.098 x 24.892 mm, distinct from the smaller printed image. Area uses the outer rectangular dimensions.

referenceLabel: doubles tennis courts within the playing lines
singularLabel: a doubles tennis court within its playing lines
assumption: A doubles tennis court is 78 by 36 feet, giving 260.87173632 square metres. This excludes run-off space, seating and surrounding facilities.
sourceNote: ITF specifies a 78-foot length and 36-foot doubles width. Area uses exact foot conversion instead of multiplying the rounded metric dimensions.

referenceLabel: the tick rate of a metronome set to 60 BPM
singularLabel: a metronome set to 60 BPM
assumption: A metronome deliberately set to 60 beats per minute ticks once per second (1 Hz). This is a chosen setting, not an average tempo.
sourceNote: Yamaha recommends starting a metronome exercise at 60 BPM. One beat per second follows from 60 seconds per minute.

referenceLabel: defined one-watt lights
singularLabel: an imagined one-watt light
assumption: Imagine a light specified to draw exactly 1 W electrically while on. This is a defined comparison prop, not a measured typical lamp; assume constant input power.
sourceNote: NIST defines one watt as one joule per second. The one-watt light is an explicitly chosen illustration, not a product specification.
